feature.title: 対局イベントの永続化と順序付き配信

source.needle: ## 確定済みの対局イベントを配信する

flow: StagedGameChange freezes canonical facts from an accepted receipt, and the PostgreSQL commit writes the receipt and outbox rows atomically.
An exclusively locked PostgreSQL session supplies the earliest pending row without holding a transaction across publication.
OutboxPublisher sends version-one JSON to the exact game channel and marks only the selected row after confirmed transport acceptance.
An uncertain send or acknowledgement leaves a retryable identity that can be published again.

guarantees.statement: Accepted receipts and canonical frozen outbox facts commit together. Rejection and same-request replay do not enqueue extra facts.
Dispatch preserves queue order and stable identity (game_id, seq, kind). Uncertain send or marking can duplicate an identity without skipping pending work.
An exact row is marked only after a nonnegative PUBLISH integer response, including zero subscribers. This confirms transport acceptance rather than subscriber delivery or durable broker storage.
One PostgreSQL session owns the publisher lock. Losing that session fails closed, and no database transaction stays open at the delivery boundary.
The publisher process owns the queue and transport, polls pending work and stops on dispatch failure or Ctrl-C.

contracts.statement: StagedGameChange validates sequence bounds and action/result consistency and freezes move-then-finish or resignation-only-finish facts.

contracts.statement: PostgresOutbox uses one nonreconnecting advisory-locked session for ordered reads and exact-row idempotent marking, rejects unsupported frozen encodings, and leaves no open transaction during transport wait.

evidence.reason: Real PostgreSQL returns the frozen move before the sequence-two finish; marking the first row twice still leaves the finish pending.
A child process cannot acquire the publisher lock until the owner drops it.
At the delivery boundary PostgreSQL reports no open transaction and another writer can commit.
Terminating the owning database session causes the old queue to fail; a replacement resumes the same pending event.
Changing a persisted event encoding version to 99 makes next_pending return Corrupt.
A real queue round trip preserves game, request and participant identifiers containing NUL and backslashes.

contracts.gap: The delivery-boundary fixture observes database state and subsequent writes. It is not an all-components test stalled on a real broker.

contracts.statement: OutboxPublisher publishes before marking. The Valkey adapter accepts only valid nonnegative PUBLISH integers and invalidates a cancelled or timed-out connection.

evidence.reason: Fake queue and transport assert publication sequence order after failed send and uncertain mark, including duplicate publication.

Cancelling publication prevents connection reuse or automatic reconnection.

contracts.gap: Transport tests use a controlled TCP RESP fixture and fake repository, not a deployed Valkey instance or subscriber.

contracts.statement: The messaging adapter encodes schema-version-one JSON with explicit event identity and a channel derived from every game-ID byte.

evidence.reason: JSON shape, event IDs, move/drop values and terminal results are directly compared.
Channel examples encode every ID byte without collisions or Pub/Sub glob characters.

contracts.gap: Subscriber delivery, subscription lifecycle and notification rejection are mapped by realtime-gameplay rather than asserted by these publication examples.

limitations: No mapped test traverses a real database, deployed Valkey and live subscriber together. No subscriber delivery or broker persistence is promised.
Standalone process startup, restart and signal behavior remain explicit gaps even though queue-lock and adapter cancellation behavior have dedicated tests.
Schema validation and database-role policy are mapped by startup-schema-isolation.
Source links and successful test execution establish traceable evidence, not semantic proof or complete coverage of these guarantees.
